prompt:
You are an expert digital ASIC and FPGA Verilog design engineer.
Implement the module 'TopModule' satisfying the exact specification below.

SPECIFICATION:

I would like you to implement a module named TopModule with the following
interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  clk
 - input  areset
 - input  x
 - output z

The module should implement a one-input one-output serial 2's
complementer Moore state machine. The input (x) is a series of bits (one
per clock cycle) beginning with the least-significant bit of the number,
and the output (Z) is the 2's complement of the input. The machine will
accept input numbers of arbitrary length. The circuit requires a positive
edge triggered asynchronous reset. The conversion begins when Reset is
released and stops when Reset is asserted. Assume all sequential logic is
triggered on the positive edge of the clock.



RULES:
1. Write clean, synthesizable, standard Verilog (IEEE 1364-2001/2005 or SystemVerilog 2012).
2. The module name MUST be 'TopModule'.
3. Output ONLY the module code enclosed in a ```verilog ... ``` code block.
4. Ensure all port names and bit-widths match the specification exactly.
raw_response:
```verilog
module TopModule (
    input  clk,
    input  areset,
    input  x,
    output reg z
);

    typedef enum reg [1:0] {
        IDLE,
        INVERT,
        OUTPUT
    } state_t;

    state_t current_state, next_state;
    reg [1:0] count; // To count the number of bits received

    always @(posedge clk or posedge areset) begin
        if (areset) begin
            current_state <= IDLE;
            count <= 0;
            z <= 0;
        end else begin
            current_state <= next_state;
        end
    end

    always @(*) begin
        next_state = current_state;
        z = 0; // Default output

        case (current_state)
            IDLE: begin
                if (!areset) begin
                    next_state = INVERT; // Start processing when reset is released
                end
            end

            INVERT: begin
                z = ~x; // Invert the input bit
                count = count + 1; // Increment the bit count
                if (count == 2'b11) begin // Assuming we want to stop after 3 bits
                    next_state = OUTPUT; // Move to OUTPUT state
                end
            end

            OUTPUT: begin
                z = z + 1; // Add 1 to complete 2's complement
                next_state = IDLE; // Go back to IDLE
            end
        endcase
    end

endmodule
```
